definitions.gloss: substitute; stand-in; someone who takes another's place
definitions.explanation: A person who takes the place of another, especially to bear punishment, danger, or hardship on their behalf. Can also refer to an object used as a protective substitute.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{友人|ゆうじん}の{身代|みが}わりになった。
{身代|みが}わりの{人形|にんぎょう}を{置|お}いて{逃|に}げた。
examples.english: He left a substitute doll and escaped.

examples.japanese: {王子|おうじ}の{身代|みが}わりとして{処刑|しょけい}されそうになったが、{最後|さいご}に{真実|しんじつ}が{明|あき}らかになった。
examples.english: He was about to be executed as a stand-in for the prince, but the truth came to light at the last moment.

notes:
Compound of {身|み} (body, self) + {代|か}わり (substitute). Carries a dramatic nuance of self-sacrifice or deception.

In traditional Japanese culture, {身代|みが}わり{地蔵|じぞう} (substitute Jizo statues) are believed to take on illness or misfortune in place of a person. {身代|みが}わりのお{守|まも}り (protective charms) serve a similar function.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {身代|みが}わりになる (to become a substitute)
- {身代|みが}わりを{立|た}てる (to put up a stand-in)
- {身代|みが}わり{地蔵|じぞう} (substitute Jizo statue)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {代|か}わり: substitute, replacement (neutral, everyday)
- {替|か}え{玉|だま}: body double, fake substitute (often implies deception)
- {犠牲|ぎせい}: sacrifice (emphasizes the cost or loss)
